clue.text: Had influence after having moved to Kensington

parts.note: having moved something means having carried it
Kensington in London has the postcode W8, read out as W-EIGHT

explanation.surface: Someone gained social clout after relocating to a smart London district.
explanation.walkthrough: Kensington is an upmarket area of west London whose postal district is W8; spoken as letters and figure, W8 gives the sound of the second word.
explanation.definitionFit: To carry weight is an idiom for having authority or sway over others.

clue.text: Suffer direly when ian goes crazy

indicators.note: crazy says the letters of the words ian goes are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone suffers terribly whenever a man called Ian loses his mind.
explanation.definitionFit: To agonise is to undergo great mental torment, to suffer acutely.

clue.text: Consider it to be the going price

explanation.surface: A note judging something to be at the current market price.
explanation.definitionFit: To rate something is to regard it as being so; a rate is also the standard charge or tariff.

clue.text: Old German prince from select, orthodox family

indicators.note: from tells us the answer is taken out of a run of the clue's own letters

explanation.surface: A German nobleman of old who comes from an exclusive, traditional family.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'select, orthodox', ignoring the comma; 'family' is surface padding.
explanation.definitionFit: Electors were the princes of the Holy Roman Empire who had a vote in choosing the emperor.

clue.text: Well-disposed to passing on one's goods

explanation.surface: Someone happy to bequeath their possessions to heirs.
explanation.definitionFit: Willing means ready and inclined; it also means leaving property to someone by a testament.

clue.text: Urge to see one-time companion

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: Someone feels a longing to visit an old friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one-time companion' looks like a single phrase meaning ex-partner, but it splits into three abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: An itch is a restless craving or desire for something.

clue.text: Regular place to dry the washing

explanation.surface: Advice about the usual spot for drying laundry.
explanation.definitionFit: A hangout is a place someone frequents; to hang out clothes is to put them on the line to dry.

clue.text: Bespoke tailors are forced to do so

definitions.text: tailors are forced to do so

explanation.surface: Custom tailors must take measurements as a matter of course.
explanation.definitionFit: Bespoke clothing is cut to the customer's size; read literally, tailors are compelled (made) to measure.

clue.text: Strangely contrived by ex-PM and quiz hostess

parts.note: Edward Heath was British Prime Minister 1970-74
Anne Robinson hosted the TV quiz The Weakest Link

explanation.surface: Something oddly concocted by a former prime minister together with a TV quizmistress.
explanation.walkthrough: W. Heath Robinson was a cartoonist famous for drawing absurdly elaborate machines, hence the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A Heath Robinson device is an over-complicated, makeshift contraption.

clue.text: A situation confronting the French evangelist

indicators.note: confronting means standing in front of, so the earlier pieces come before the next

parts.note: a post is a job or situation
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A position facing a French preacher.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostle is a missionary who spreads the Christian gospel.

clue.text: Leave a publican to apply for it

definitions.text: a publican to apply for it

explanation.surface: Instructions for a pub landlord to seek permission.
explanation.definitionFit: Licence means permission or leave; a pub landlord must hold a licence to sell alcohol.

clue.text: About to get retirement home in Ireland

indicators.note: retirement means going backwards, so the word for about is read in reverse

parts.note: re means about or concerning
in means at home

explanation.surface: Someone about to retire to a house in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Erin is the old poetic name for Ireland.

clue.text: Remained utterly sober

indicators.note: utterly here means when uttered or spoken, signalling a soundalike

parts.note: remained means stayed

explanation.surface: Someone kept completely off the drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'utterly' looks like an intensifier meaning totally; it is read as 'when uttered'.
explanation.definitionFit: Staid means serious and restrained, a synonym of sober in manner.

clue.text: Dash to secure the door

explanation.surface: A rush to lock up.
explanation.definitionFit: To bolt is to run off suddenly, and also to fasten a door with a sliding bar.

clue.text: A temperate chap in charge of Greek

parts.note: TT means teetotal, describing someone who abstains from alcohol

explanation.surface: A sober man who runs the Greek department.
explanation.definitionFit: Attic is the ancient Greek dialect of Athens, the classical literary form of the language.

clue.text: Drank back in HQ

indicators.note: back means the word for drank is written right to left

parts.note: toped means drank alcohol to excess

explanation.surface: Drinking returned to at headquarters.
explanation.definitionFit: A depot is a base or headquarters, especially a military one.

clue.text: New senator given only modest rating

indicators.note: new says the letters of senator are formed into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A newly elected senator gets a poor review.
explanation.definitionFit: A single star in reviews or hotel grading is a low, basic score.

clue.text: Greek diner is comparatively grand

parts.note: a diner is an eater

explanation.surface: A Greek restaurant patron seems rather posh.
explanation.definitionFit: Greater is the comparative form of great, meaning bigger or grander.

clue.text: Smoothing things out late in the day

explanation.surface: Settling differences toward nightfall.
explanation.definitionFit: Evening means levelling or making even; it is also the time after afternoon.

clue.text: Somehow find fee for a Turkish man

indicators.note: somehow says the letters of find fee come out in some other order

explanation.surface: Somehow locating money for a man from Turkey.
explanation.definitionFit: Effendi is a Turkish title of respect for a man of education or standing.

clue.text: Escapes punishment and leaves

explanation.surface: Someone avoids a penalty and departs.
explanation.definitionFit: To get off is to be let off a charge, and also to depart or alight.

clue.text: Saw rambler go into the lead

indicators.note: go into means the word for rambler is placed inside the chemical symbol

parts.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for the metal lead
a rover is someone who wanders

explanation.surface: A hiker looks at someone going to the front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' is not a past tense but a noun: an old saying.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is a traditional saying or maxim.

clue.text: Offered to sell after being exploited

parts.note: put up means offered for sale, as at auction
on can mean after, as in on arrival

explanation.surface: An item offered for sale after someone took advantage.
explanation.definitionFit: Put-upon describes someone imposed on or taken advantage of.

clue.text: Recluse appears before young child

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
a mite is a small child

explanation.surface: A hermit shows up ahead of a little one.
explanation.definitionFit: An eremite is a hermit, a religious solitary.

clue.text: Peter was in madras a few days ago

indicators.note: was in tells us the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A man called Peter was in the Indian city of Madras recently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peter' looks like a man's name but is criminal slang for a strongbox; Madras is the former name of Chennai.
explanation.definitionFit: In underworld slang a peter is a strongbox that thieves crack.

clue.text: National express

explanation.surface: A two-word phrase like the name of a coach company.
explanation.definitionFit: State means national, as in state schools; to state is to express in words.

clue.text: Poor to average

explanation.surface: A slide from bad to middling.
explanation.definitionFit: Mean means of low quality or shabby; as a noun it is an average value.

clue.text: Fashionable place of worship on an island

parts.note: in means fashionable
CH is an abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A trendy chapel on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: Inch is a Scottish word for a small island, found in many place names.
explanation.definitionFit: Inch, from Gaelic innis, names a small island in Scotland.

clue.text: Only a fish

explanation.surface: Just a single fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Sole means single or only, and is also a flatfish.

clue.text: Met — with an accident

explanation.surface: Someone encountered misfortune.
explanation.definitionFit: To run into someone is to meet them by chance, and also to collide with something.

clue.text: Clause limiting poor vi's movements

indicators.note: movements means the letters of poor vi's are moved around

parts.note: the apostrophe is ignored and the letters VIS are used

explanation.surface: A rule restricting the actions of a poor woman named Vi.
explanation.definitionFit: A proviso is a condition attached to an agreement that restricts it.

clue.text: Likely to steal thunder from heavy-handed pianist

definitions.text: Likely to steal thunder from heavy-handed pianist

parts.words: Likely to steal thunder from heavy-handed pianist
parts.note: a nimble keyboard player would outshine a clumsy one, and nimble-handed also describes a pickpocket

explanation.surface: A deft musician outshines a clumsy one at the keyboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with delicate, quick fingers plays deftly and also pilfers easily.
